title: Extend depth sweep: DEPTH=10 -> 12
description: Set DEPTH=12 (model_dim 768, 6 heads); reduced DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE 128->64 (grad_accum doubled 2->4) to keep VRAM headroom vs depth=10's 66.5GB.
reflection: Regressed sharply: val_bpb 1.016254, worse than both the depth=10 baseline (1.002279) and the original depth=8 baseline (1.014027). Peak VRAM was only 49.0GB, well under budget, meaning the DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE cut to 64 was unnecessary caution and likely hurt via lower MFU (smaller batches -> more kernel-launch/overhead per token, fewer effective tokens processed in the fixed 300s wall-clock budget) on top of depth=12 having more FLOPs/token. Can't cleanly separate 'depth=12 hurts' from 'batch-size-64 hurts' from this run alone. Recommend: do NOT extend depth further without keeping DEVICE_BATCH_SIZE=128 (VRAM clearly wasn't the constraint), and treat depth=10 as the local optimum for this time budget unless someone reruns depth=12 at batch=128 to isolate the two effects.
